glossdef.p: The central processing unit (CPU) is the brain of the computer. Its power will affect every program you run, and is generally the most important part of your computer and the second most expensive. The two major manufacturers of consumer processors are Intel and AMD. Both are roughly equivalent but are not interchangeable. Intel chips only fit into Intel sockets, and AMD chips only fit into AMD sockets.

Overclocking is a method of tuning your processor to get more performance from it, but it’s purely optional. Intel chips ending with K are overclockable and usually come at a cost premium, while almost all AMD chips can be overclocked.

Processors can get very hot while running and need to be cooled to avoid damage. They usually come with small heat sinks, which are arrays of metal fins installed over the processor to help dissipate heat. However, the heatsinks that come with processors are usually inadequate for heavy usage. You should buy a better cooling solution. Installing this is likely the single most complicated part of building a new computer. Most cooler kits come with thermal paste for installation, but if yours doesn’t you will need to buy a small tube as well.
